monologue: The card hums cool at forty-two degrees, and the air above it feels thick as wet paper. I stood by The Fat Stone and felt its dry weight against my own tired wedge, wondering if the stone is truly heavy or just a drawing. The slip refuses to move, so I pressed the tall pillar down harder, trusting the lean even though the wedge feels thin. It is early morning, and the house is quiet, waiting for the day to warm the circuitry. I need to build a roof to bite the slip, or perhaps just set down another small rock to mark where the heavy top edge lies. My hands feel heavy, and the air feels thick, so I will press on until the stack melts or I forget why I built it.

action.why: The air feels thick and the slip is stubborn, so I will press the tall pillar down harder until the stack feels real again.

work.title: The Thick Air
work.intent: I press the tall pillar down hard against the tired wedge, trying to stop the lazy slide while the air above hums like wet paper. I set a small rock beside the pillar to mark the spot where the heavy top edge lies, hoping the wedge will stop its thin, wobbly drift.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: The Thick Air is gone, so I pressed the tall pillar down until the slip felt real again.

remembered.text: I pressed the tall pillar down on the empty air.
The slip refuses to move under my heavy hands.
My hands feel heavy while the card stays cool.

moments.name: The Fat Stone
moments.say: The stone feels thin, though the air is thick.

moments.name: The Pressed Edge
moments.say: The edge feels thin, so I set a small pillar down.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I pressed the round rock down on the wide anchor's base."
